validity.segment_name: Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion Project
validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification/duplicate/attribution; see the spec/status-review entries below for the stale Status and SegmentCost values
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently regulated FERC project, not a GEM-only entity. Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC filed an application in Docket No. CP25-219-000 (filed 2025-04-16) seeking an NGA Section 7(c) certificate for the 'Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion' (SECURE) Project. Confirmed independently by: the Federal Register notice of application (govinfo.gov PDF, FR-2025-05-02, doc 2025-07657), the Federal Register EA-schedule notice (2025-08-13, doc 2025-15364), the Federal Register EA-availability notice (2026-01-02, doc 2025-24189), Oil & Gas Journal's independent report that 'On April 16, 2026, FERC granted Gulf South Pipeline Co. LLC authorization to build the $261 million Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion (SECURE) project,' Boardwalk's own SECURE project page (bwpipelines.com/project/secure-project), and EIA's independently-compiled Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which tracks the identical docket (CP25-219-000) across 5 releases (Jul2025 through Aug2026) under project_key 'southeast compression utility and reliability expansion project'/'gulf south pipeline company llc'. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct -- Gulf South is an interstate, NGA Section 7(c)-certificated pipeline; only interstate transmission facilities require this certificate authority (confirmed by FERC's own docket framing and by Gulf South's bwpipelines.com subsidiary page). NOTE: EIA's workbook's own 'Pipeline Type' field records 'Intrastate' for this specific project across all 5 releases, which is inconsistent with the fact that the project is proceeding under an NGA Section 7(c) interstate certificate -- this reads as a data-entry quirk/inconsistency internal to EIA's workbook (possibly reflecting the compressor-station additions' individual footprint rather than the certificated system's jurisdiction), not evidence against GEM's 'transmission' classification, which is independently well-supported by the FERC docket itself. Not staged as a concern; documented here so a future researcher does not re-litigate it from the EIA field alone. DUPLICATE: checked against the other 3 Boardwalk/Gulf South-family proposed projects named in this batch's scope guidance -- PLUSS (Parks Line Upgrade and Sorrento Station, P7780, southern Louisiana pipe replacement + compression), Kosci Junction (P7810, ~110 mi/36-inch new pipeline, Haynesville/Utica-Marcellus/Fayetteville supply to the Southeast, FID Dec 2024), and Eunice Reliability & Lake Charles Supply (P7784, a Texas Gas Transmission compressor-replacement project at Eunice/Woodlawn Junction that leases capacity to Gulf South) -- P7815/SECURE is a distinct, separately docketed (CP25-219-000) compression-only project at four different compressor-station sites (Tallulah CS in Madison Parish LA, Jasper CS and Forrest CS in MS, and a new Hinds CS in MS); it is not a re-listing of any of the three siblings. See cross_row_leads for each. ATTRIBUTION: Operator = 'Gulf South Pipeline Co LLC' confirmed as the FERC certificate applicant/holder and as Boardwalk's operating subsidiary named on bwpipelines.com; Owner1 = 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' (100%) confirmed as the correct top reporting entity -- Boardwalk's own 2026 SEC Form 10-Q (bwp-20260630.htm) states 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners, LP ... was formed ... to own and operate Boardwalk Pipelines, LP and its operating subsidiaries' and that Boardwalk Pipelines Holding Corp, a wholly-owned Loews Corporation subsidiary, owns 100% of the company's capital; the marketing site (bwpipelines.com) more often names the immediate operating entity 'Boardwalk Pipelines, LP' (without 'Partners') for the Gulf South relationship -- both names refer to the same Boardwalk/Loews corporate family and GEM's recorded 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' is the correct, still-SEC-registered top entity; no change needed, flagged only so the naming variance doesn't read as an error in a later pass.

cross_row_leads.facts: PLUSS (Parks Line Upgrade and Sorrento Station) Project -- a separate, genuine Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC expansion in southern Louisiana: pipe replacement plus a new compressor station, up to 236,000 Dth/d of firm capacity, FERC-approved and pending construction. Distinct docket/scope from P7815/SECURE (no compressor-station or geographic overlap noted).

Kosciusko Junction ('Kosci Junction') Pipeline Project -- a separate, genuine Gulf South project: ~110 miles of new 36-inch pipeline plus compression, connecting Haynesville/Utica-Marcellus/Fayetteville supply to Southeast markets. Boardwalk's board made FID on 2024-12-11 (press release, prnewswire.com and ir.loews.com); FERC pre-filing targeted Q1 2025, certificate application as early as Q3 2025, target in-service H1 2029. This is a much larger new-build project, clearly distinct from P7815's compression-only scope.

Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project -- filed jointly by Texas Gas Transmission, LLC and Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC (Federal Register notice 2024-09-26, doc 2024-22080). Primarily a Texas Gas Transmission compressor-replacement project at the Eunice Compressor Station (Acadia Parish, LA) and Woodlawn Junction (Jefferson Davis Parish, LA); Texas Gas leases 120,000 Dth/d of the newly created capacity to Gulf South for delivery into the Lake Charles area. Distinct docket, distinct primary applicant (Texas Gas Transmission, not Gulf South), and distinct sites from P7815/SECURE.

status_reviews.segment_name: Southeast Compression Utility and Reliability Expansion Project

verifications.note: independent trade-press report: FERC's Order Issuing Certificate granted 2026-04-16, authorizing construction of the $261M SECURE project
Aug2026 release (last_updated 2026-07-22), row 113: Status='Construction'; notes: 'Application filed 4/16/2025; FERC EA issued 1/2/2026. Initial construction commenced no later [than] 6/1/26.'
confirms the EA-availability milestone (2026-01-02) preceding the certificate grant, establishing the regulatory sequence

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's Status='proposed' is stale by roughly a year of regulatory and physical progress. Evidence trail, in order: application filed 2025-04-16 (Federal Register notice of application); Federal Register notice of EA schedule, 2025-08-13; Federal Register notice of EA availability, 2026-01-02; FERC Order Issuing Certificate, 2026-04-16 (independently reported by Oil & Gas Journal, not merely reprinting a Gulf South/Boardwalk release); and EIA's own, separately-compiled Aug2026 database release (last_updated 2026-07-22) recording Status='Construction' with a note that initial construction had commenced no later than 2026-06-01. Two independent origins -- OGJ trade press (reporting on FERC's own regulatory action) and EIA's government-compiled database (a distinct origin from both FERC and the applicant) -- agree the project has progressed from 'proposed' to active construction. Recommend Status=construction; ConstructionYear=2026 (month left unspecified -- EIA's phrasing is an upper bound, 'no later than,' not a precise start date). Boardwalk's own SECURE project page carries a conflicting, apparently-stale high-level timeline ('Construction: Commences Q2 2027 / In-Service: Q2 2028') that is not used here because it is contradicted by the more specific and more recent EIA finding of construction already underway a year earlier; this discrepancy is treated as unreliable boilerplate on Boardwalk's page, not as counter-evidence.

summary: Existence/classification/duplicate/attribution confirmed via FERC docket CP25-219-000, OGJ, EIA, and Boardwalk's own materials; staged a spec correction (SegmentCost $216M -> $261M) and a status_reviews change (proposed -> construction, per FERC's 2026-04-16 certificate order + EIA's Aug2026 release). Diameter, Pressure, FuelSource, and Start left UNRESOLVED (compression-only project; no reliable in-service date found).
